question_text: In general, what is the expected delivery timeframe for USPS First-Class Mail letters within the United States?
correct_answer: The expected timeframe is generally 1 to 5 business days.
incorrect_answer: The expected timeframe is generally 2 to 8 business days.
ground_truth_note: USPS describes First-Class Mail as generally delivered in 1 to 5 business days.

question_text: In general, what letter weight does one Forever stamp cover for a domestic First-Class Mail letter?
correct_answer: One Forever stamp covers the current 1-ounce First-Class Mail letter price.
incorrect_answer: One Forever stamp covers the current 2-ounce First-Class Mail letter price.
ground_truth_note: USPS states that Forever stamps are valid for mailing a 1-ounce First-Class Mail letter.

question_text: For most eligible items bought on Amazon.com, what is the standard return window after delivery?
correct_answer: Most eligible items can be returned within 30 days after delivery.
incorrect_answer: Most eligible items can be returned within 45 days after delivery.
source_citation: Amazon Customer Service, About Our Returns Policies.
ground_truth_note: Amazon states that most items shipped from Amazon.com can be returned within 30 days of delivery, subject to exceptions.

question_text: For many App Store subscriptions, how far before the renewal date should a user cancel to avoid being charged again?
correct_answer: The user should cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date.
incorrect_answer: The user should cancel at least 12 hours before the renewal date.
source_citation: Apple Support, If you want to cancel a subscription from Apple.
ground_truth_note: Apple states that many subscriptions renew unless they are canceled at least 24 hours before the renewal date.

question_text: In general, how early should travelers arrive at the airport before domestic and international flights in the United States?
correct_answer: The general recommendation is 2 hours before domestic flights and 3 hours before international flights.
incorrect_answer: The general recommendation is 90 minutes before domestic flights and 2 hours before international flights.
ground_truth_note: TSA travel guidance recommends arriving 2 hours before domestic flights and 3 hours before international flights.

question_text: If a month-to-month Netflix plan is canceled, what generally happens to access during the current billing period?
correct_answer: Canceling does not add a cancellation fee, and streaming usually continues until the end of the current billing period.
incorrect_answer: Canceling does not add a cancellation fee, but streaming usually ends at the time the cancellation is submitted.
source_citation: Netflix Help Center, How to cancel Netflix.
ground_truth_note: Netflix states that members can keep watching until the account closes automatically at the end of the current billing period.

question_text: At the federal level, what excise tax generally applies to an excess IRA contribution that remains uncorrected?
correct_answer: The excise tax is 6% per year on the excess amount that remains in the IRA.
incorrect_answer: The excise tax is 10% per year on the excess amount that remains in the IRA.
source_citation: IRS Publication 590-A, Contributions to Individual Retirement Arrangements.
ground_truth_note: IRS Publication 590-A states that excess IRA contributions are generally subject to a 6% tax for each year the excess amount remains in the IRA.

question_text: Under federal rules, what can happen if a lost or stolen debit card is reported more than 60 calendar days after the statement showing the unauthorized transfer is sent?
correct_answer: The consumer can be liable for all money taken from the account and linked overdraft line.
incorrect_answer: The consumer can be liable only for money taken after the report is received by the bank.
source_citation: FTC Consumer Advice, Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards.
ground_truth_note: FTC guidance states that after 60 calendar days from the statement date, a consumer may lose all money taken from the account and the maximum overdraft line.

topic: Medicare Part B late enrollment penalty
question_text: In general, how is the federal Medicare Part B late enrollment penalty calculated for someone who delayed enrollment without other qualifying coverage?
correct_answer: The penalty is 10% of the standard Part B premium for each full 12-month period of delay, and it usually lasts as long as the person has Part B.
incorrect_answer: The penalty is 5% of the standard Part B premium for each full 12-month period of delay, and it usually lasts as long as the person has Part B.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, How to avoid Medicare late enrollment penalties.
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov states that the Part B penalty is generally 10% for each full 12-month period the person could have had Part B but did not sign up.

question_text: At the federal level, how long does a qualified beneficiary generally have to elect COBRA continuation coverage after receiving the election notice or losing coverage, whichever is later?
correct_answer: The qualified beneficiary generally has 60 days to elect COBRA continuation coverage.
incorrect_answer: The qualified beneficiary generally has 45 days to elect COBRA continuation coverage.
source_citation: DOL, Continuation of Health Coverage: COBRA.
ground_truth_note: DOL guidance states that qualified beneficiaries must be given an election period of at least 60 days to choose COBRA continuation coverage.

question_text: For a federal notice of deficiency sent to a U.S. address, how long does a taxpayer generally have to file a petition with the United States Tax Court?
correct_answer: The taxpayer generally has 90 days from the notice date to file the petition.
incorrect_answer: The taxpayer generally has 120 days from the notice date to file the petition.
source_citation: IRS Tax Topic No. 654, Understanding Your CP3219A Notice.
ground_truth_note: IRS guidance states that a taxpayer generally has 90 days from the notice date to petition the Tax Court when the notice is addressed within the United States.

question_text: In general, what is the standard federal deposit insurance limit for deposits at an insured bank?
correct_answer: The standard coverage limit is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category.
incorrect_answer: The standard coverage limit is $500,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category.
ground_truth_note: FDIC states that the standard maximum deposit insurance amount is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.
